Schooler et al. (2004) — acute attentional reset on initial nature engagement; chronic re-engagement requires habit formation (weeks to sustain without novelty decay)

McEwen (1998) — allostatic load theory: acute stress response (seconds-to-hours) is reversible physiological adaptation; chronic stress (days-to-months sustained) produces allostatic overload and system degradation

NEUROMOD-I C-11 — chronic restoration formula: T29 specifies that T_restoration effects (cortisol recovery, NE baseline resetting) require sustained exposure time ≥7 days; acute exposure does not engage chronic restoration pathway
